cases.given: A fresh SQLite database with no users table.
cases.when: The existing standalone database initializer runs, then an account with display name, email, supplied password-hash value and one supported role is inserted without specifying an ID.
cases.then: Initialization succeeds; users has id as an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and the required account columns with the specified SQLite types and constraints; the inserted account has a generated, stable integer ID and its supplied field values are stored.

cases.given: A database initialized with the replacement users table and a valid account.
cases.when: Account inserts are attempted with each required field NULL, with a duplicate email, and with an unsupported role; valid accounts are inserted using each of the three supported roles.
cases.then: Each invalid insert is rejected without adding an account; valid inserts succeed with exactly one stored role from employee, technician or administrator and retain the supplied password-hash value. The table has no plaintext-password column.

cases.given: An existing SQLite database whose users table has the old id/name/email-only schema, once with a stored account and once empty.
cases.when: The standalone initializer runs against each database.
cases.then: Initialization exits unsuccessfully, identifies the incompatibility and provides actionable backup or explicit-reset guidance without an exact-wording assertion; the old table definition and any stored rows remain unchanged, and the database is accessible after failed initialization.

cases.given: A database with the replacement users schema and an account with a known ID and field values.
cases.then: Initialization succeeds; the account, ID, field values and replacement schema remain unchanged, and another valid account can still be inserted and read.
